rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent a messenger to every community and generation, just as Muhammad was sent to his own community.
rows.anchor: كما بعثناك يا محمد رسولا إلى أمتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن explains the message: worship God and shun worship of the taghut, meaning Satan and anyone who calls people to error.
rows.anchor: وأن هذه هي المفسرة ويعني بالطاغوت الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided some by granting the favor He knew would lead them to believe; they believed, so that favor is called guidance.
rows.anchor: بأن لطف له بما علم أنه يؤمن عنده فآمن فسمى ذلك اللطف هداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi also allows that the phrase means God guided them to Paradise through their faith.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد منهم فمنهم من هداه الله إلى الجنة بإيمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects guidance here as merely presenting proofs, since God made proofs equally available to believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يريد بالهداية هنا نصب الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Thamud verse is cited to contrast guidance as showing proofs with the guidance meant here.
rows.anchor: فأما ثمود فهديناهم [فصلت: 17]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some turned away from the messenger's call, so God forsook them; error became fixed and they would never believe.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من أعرض عما دعاه إليه الرسول فخذله الله فثبتت عليه الضلالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes the fixed misguidance to mean the punishment and destruction that became due.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه وجبت عليه الضلالة وهي العذاب والهلاك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan explains the phrase as the punishment for misguidance becoming due to them.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حقت عليه عقوبة الضلالة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are told to travel through the lands of those punished for disbelief and see their fate, lest they follow the same path and suffer likewise.
rows.anchor: أرض المكذبين الذين عاقبهم الله إن لم تصدقوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement consoles Muhammad: their failure to believe is not his fault; their immersion in disbelief means they will never believe, and God leaves them astray as previously explained.
rows.anchor: هذا تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعائه لمن لا يفلح بالإجابة

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَن يُضِلُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi says the verse's divine misguidance is not the doctrine of compulsion attributed to the Jabriyya.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا بيان أن الإضلال في الآية ليس المراد به ما ذكره أهل الجبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will have no helper to rescue them from punishment.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم من ناصر ينصرهم ويخلصهم من العقاب

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة ويعقوب وسهل وخلف
rows.claim: These readers use the second-person تاء in ألم تروا; the others use ياء, which addresses the previously mentioned unbelievers, while تاء connects to the preceding address about God's gifts.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة ويعقوب وسهل وخلف { ألم تروا } بالتاء

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وابن عامر
rows.claim: Kufans and Ibn Amir read ظعنكم with a still عين; the remaining readers use its open vowel, and both are Arabic forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الكوفة وابن عامر ظعنكم ساكنة العين والباقون بفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms ظعن and ظعن are dialect variants, like النهر and النهر and الشمع and الشمع.
rows.anchor: والظعن والظعن بفتح العين وسكونها لغتان ومثله النهر والنهر

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's line uses الظعن with an open عين, witnessing this vocalized form.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: فقد أشرب الراح

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects treating the still-vowel form as a lightening of the open form, comparing it to words that do not undergo such general reduction.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: ولا يجوز أن يكون الظعن مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form of أمهات is أمات; the ه was added for emphasis, as in أهرقت, whose original form is أرقت.
rows.anchor: الأمهات أصله الأمات ولكن الهاء زيدت مؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفئدة is the plural of فؤاد, like أغربة from غراب; it has no plural فئدان on the pattern used for غربان.
rows.anchor: والأفئدة جمع فؤاد كما يقال غراب وأغربة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines الجو as the air high above the ground; beyond it are السكاك and اللوح, with سكاكة as a singular of السكاك.
rows.anchor: الجو الهواء البعيد من الأرض وأبعد منه السكاك واللوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's line uses الجو in the phrase هواء الجو, illustrating the word's sense of the upper air.
rows.anchor: ويلمها في هواء الجو طالبة ولا كهذا الذي في الأرض مطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السكن can mean anything one settles in, and it can also mean a dwelling.
rows.anchor: والسكن كل ما يسكن إليه والسكن أيضا المسكن

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes: السكن with open كاف means a house, while with still كاف it means the household.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: السكن بفتح الكاف الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites a hadith saying that one pomegranate can satisfy the household.
rows.anchor: " إن الرمانة لتشبع السكن "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word derives from stillness; a knife is named سكين because it stills the slaughtered animal's movement.
rows.anchor: وأصله من السكون الذي هو ضد الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أثاث means abundant household goods, from أثيث for abundant, thick growth; like متاع, it has no singular form.
rows.anchor: والأثاث متاع البيت الكثير من قولهم شعر أثيث

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The continuation of an unnamed poet's line uses أثاث, illustrating the term for household goods.
rows.anchor: بذي الرئي الجميل من الأثاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase لا تعلمون شيئا is a circumstantial clause attached to the second-person pronoun; شيئا can be a cognate accusative meaning no knowledge, or an object if تعلمون means تعرفون.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال من الكاف والميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شيئا may be parsed as an accusative cognate object for لا تعلمون علما, or as the object of تعلمون understood as تعرفون.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا ويكون تعلمون بمعنى تعرفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أثاثا and متاعا are accusatives governed by جعل.
rows.anchor: وأثاثا ومتاعا نصب بجعل أي يجعل لكم أثاثا ومتاعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought people from their mothers' wombs while they knew none of their benefits or harms, then gave them sound senses as routes to knowledge and hearts as the seat of understanding so they would thank Him.
rows.anchor: منعما عليكم بذلك وأنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and sight are sound faculties that lead to knowledge of perceptions; hearts are the place of knowledge by which people understand things.
rows.anchor: بالحواس الصحيحة التي هي طرق إلى العلم بالمدركات وتفضل عليكم بالقلوب التي تفقهون بها الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose is that people thank and praise God for these gifts.
rows.anchor: أي لكي تشكروه على ذلك وتحمدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds are fashioned to travel up, down, back, and forth through the sky, made capable of flying on their wings without depending on another support.
rows.anchor: كيف خلقها الله خلقة يمكنها معها التصرف في جو السماء صاعدة ومنحدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps birds from falling by sustaining the air beneath them, like water beneath a swimmer; this figuratively counts as holding them, though their actual remaining aloft is their own action.
rows.anchor: فيمسك الهواء تحت الطير حتى لا ينزل فيه كإمساك الماء تحت السابح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds show that they have a governor and director who can do anything; God created them as an occasion for people to reflect and attain offered reward, beyond the goodness of mere beneficence.
rows.anchor: أن لها مسخرا ومدبرا لا يعجزه شيء ولا يتعذر عليه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are signs of God's oneness and power, benefiting those who believe.
rows.anchor: لأنهم الذين انتفعوا به

words: وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنۢ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَنًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provided homes made from stone and mud, creating the wood, materials, and tools used to roof and build them.
rows.anchor: موضعا تسكنون فيه مما يتخذ من الحجر والمدر

words: وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ بُيُوتًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animal-skin homes are leather tents and domes that are light to carry on journeys.
rows.anchor: أي قبابا وخياما يخف عليكم حملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means your day of moving from one place to another; alternatively it describes nomads seeking pasture or water.
rows.anchor: أي ارتحالكم من مكان إلى مكان وقيل معنى الظعن سير أهل البوادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tents are light and convenient both while traveling and while settled.
rows.anchor: اليوم الذي تنزلون موضعا تقيمون فيه أي لا يثقل عليكم في الحالتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wool is from sheep, camel hair from camels, and hair from goats.
rows.anchor: وهي للضأن { وأوبارها } وهي للإبل { وأشعارها } وهي للمعز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses أثاث as wealth; other explanations call it household furnishings such as bedding, rugs, clothing, and coverings, which are close in sense.
rows.anchor: مالا عن ابن عباس وقيل نوعا من متاع البيت من الفراش والأكسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These materials provide enjoyments and a livelihood through trade.
rows.anchor: تتمتعون به ومعاشا تتجرون فيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan takes the term to last until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إلى يوم القيامة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the term to last until death.
rows.anchor: إلى وقت الموت عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other possibilities are the death of the owner, the death of the livestock, or the time when the goods wear out.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون أراد به موت المالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The goods are temporary, so a sensible person should not prefer them to the blessings of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنها فانية فلا ينبغي للعاقل أن يختارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is linked to God's call to Moses from the tree in the account at 28:30.
rows.anchor: إني أنا الله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to cast down the staff is linked to the sign in 7:117.
rows.anchor: وأن ألق عصاك [الأعراف: 117]

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Moses saw a green tree blazing with white fire, heard the angels glorifying God, and saw a great light; neither the greenery quenched the fire nor the fire burned it. He was bewildered, recognized a supernatural sign, received calm, and was called.
rows.anchor: شجرة خضراء من أسفلها إلى أعلاها تتوقد فيها نار بيضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated pronoun strengthens the evidence, removes doubt, and establishes certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: وإنما كرر الكناية لتأكيد الدلالة وإزالة الشبهة وتحقيق المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to remove the two sandals.
rows.anchor: أي انزعهما

rows.speaker: كعب وعكرمة والصادق
rows.claim: One explanation says the sandals were made of the hide of a dead donkey; this is attributed to Ka'b and Ikrima and also transmitted from al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: أنهما كانتا من جلد حمار ميت عن كعب وعكرمة

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وابن جريج
rows.claim: Another explanation says the sandals were from a properly slaughtered cow; Moses was told to remove them so his feet could touch the blessed valley's ground.
rows.anchor: كانتا من جلد بقرة ذكية ولكنه أمر بخلعهما ليباشر بقدميه الأرض

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Bare feet signify humility; the early generations therefore performed circumambulation barefoot.
rows.anchor: أن الحفاء من علامة التواضع ولذلك كانت السلف تطوف حفاة عن الأصم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Moses had worn sandals to avoid impurity and insects; God reassured him that he was safe and the place was pure.
rows.anchor: اتقاء من الأنجاس وخوفا من الحشرات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the sacred valley as blessed, with abundant provision and fertility.
rows.anchor: المبارك عن ابن عباس بورك فيه بسعة الرزق والخصب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss takes المقدس to mean purified.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المطهر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجبائي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Jubba'i take طوى as the valley's proper name.
rows.anchor: هو اسم الوادي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والجبائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the valley was named طوى because it was sanctified twice, as if folded twice in blessing.
rows.anchor: سمي به لأن الوادي قدس مرتين فكأنه طوي بالبركة مرتين عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Moses for the prophetic mission and told him to listen carefully and steadily to the revelation; after announcing his prophethood, He instructed him to hear the revelation.
rows.anchor: إليك من كلامي واصغ إليه وتثبت

words: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God deserves worship; He commands Moses to worship Him alone, without associating anyone, and to convey this to his people.
rows.anchor: أي لا إله يستحق العبادة غيري

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Hasan and Mujahid understand this as praying so that one remembers God through glorifying and magnifying Him.
rows.anchor: لأن الصلاة لا تكون إلا بذكر الله عن الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God will remember Moses with praise and commendation.
rows.anchor: لأن أذكرك بالمدح والثناء

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads it as a command to pray to God alone, rather than praying as idolaters do.
rows.anchor: صل لي ولا تصل لغيري كما يفعله المشركون عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Most commentators, and a report from Abu Ja'far, take it as a command to perform a prayer whenever one remembers it, whether or not its appointed time has arrived.
rows.anchor: أقم الصلاة متى ذكرت أن عليك صلاة كنت في وقتها أم لم تكن

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: The commentary says this final interpretation is supported by a report from Anas back to the Prophet, but the excerpt gives no report text.
rows.anchor: ويعضده ما رواه أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads أشدد with hamza of قطع and an open hamza, and أشركه with a damma; the other readers use hamzat al-wasl and fatḥ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر أشدد بقطع الهمزة وفتحها وأشركه بضمها

rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو البرهسم
rows.claim: In noncanonical readings, Ikrima has وأهس with sin, while Abu al-Barhasm has وأهش with a kasra under the ه.
rows.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة عكرمة وأهس بالسين وقراءة أبي البرهسم وأهش بكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir's reading makes أشدد indicative, while the others make it a supplication; the damma in أشركه is very weak because Moses cannot himself make Aaron a prophet, so fatḥ as a prayer is fitting.
rows.anchor: الوجه في قراءة أبي عامر أنه جعله خبرا وسائر القراء جعلوه دعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra in أهش may represent the damma form, meaning to strike fodder for the sheep; Arabic also has paired intransitive and transitive forms like يهر ويهره and يشد ويشده.
rows.anchor: أراد أهش بضم الهاء أي أكسر الكلاء بها للغنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أهس means to drive; although one would expect أهس بها غنمي, the preposition عليها follows the sense of driving them toward and along with her.
rows.anchor: وأما أهس بالسين فمعناه أسوق وكان ينبغي أن يقول أهس بها غنمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التوكؤ and الاتكاء mean the same; الهش is beating tree leaves down, and مآرب means needs, with مأربة having three possible vowelings.
rows.anchor: التوكؤ والاتكاء بمعنى مثل التوقي والاتقاء والهش ضرب ورق الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: السيرة and الطريقة are synonyms and denote a thing's passage along a direction.
rows.anchor: والسيرة والطريقة من النظائر ومعناه مرور الشيء في جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جناح derives from جنوح, inclination in flight; a person's arm is his wing because it lets the hand incline as its owner wishes. Another explanation refers to the flank because of the ribs' bend.
rows.anchor: وأصل الجناح من الجنوح وهو الميل لأن الطائر يميل به في طيرانه

rows.speaker: الراجز
rows.claim: A rajaz poet uses الجناح in a line about drawing something to the chest and side.
rows.anchor: أضمها للصدر والجناح

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the two wings mean the two sides.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الجناحان الناحيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طغيان is exceeding the limit in disobedience.
rows.anchor: والطغيان تجاوز الحد في العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: شرح الصدر means expansion, just as explaining a meaning means spreading out the account of it.
rows.anchor: وشرح الصدر توسعه ومنه شرح المعنى وهو بسط القول فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العقدة is a compacted whole that is difficult to untie; its opposite حل is like separating or cutting.
rows.anchor: والعقدة جملة مجتمعة يصعب تفكيكها والحل ضد العقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A minister bears the ruler's burden; the word is linked to وزر, burden, and to أزر, back or support, as in أزرني فلان, he supported me.
rows.anchor: والوزير حامل الثقل عن الرئيس مشتق من الوزر الذي هو الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source further relates الميزر, الإزار, and التأزير to the back or to strengthening, and allows the forms أزر and وزر to alternate like أرخ and ورخ.
rows.anchor: والإزار لأنه يسيل على الظهر والتأزير التقوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The example in 6:100 illustrates a construction in which the second object of this verb pattern precedes the first.
rows.anchor: في أن المفعول الثاني من هذا الباب قد تقدم على المفعول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If هارون is read nominative, it can be the predicate of an omitted subject: asked who the minister is, one answers, 'He is Aaron.'
rows.anchor: ولو قرأ بالرفع هارون لكان خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كثيرا can qualify an omitted verbal noun, meaning abundant glorification and remembrance, or an omitted time expression, meaning a long time spent glorifying and remembering.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا نعت مصدر محذوف في الموضعين أي تسبيحا كثيرا وذكرا كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks about the staff in Moses' hand to draw his attention to it and let the ensuing miracle occur after he has examined it.
rows.anchor: سأله عما في يده من العصا تنبيها له عليها ليقع المعجز بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he leans on his staff when walking; التوكؤ is putting one's weight on the staff while walking.
rows.anchor: أي أعتمد عليها إذا مشيت والتوكؤ التحامل على العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He strikes leaves from trees with the staff so that his sheep can eat them.
rows.anchor: أي وأخبط بها ورق الشجر لترعاه غنمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means other needs; he names the staff's regular use and alludes to its incidental uses.
rows.anchor: أي حاجات أخرى فنص على اللازم وكنى عن العارض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas lists the staff's other uses: carrying provisions; producing water when planted in the ground and food when striking it; driving off predators; fighting enemies; extending into a bucket for drawing water; shining at night; speaking and keeping Moses company; and bending high branches with its crook.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان يحمل عليها زاده ويركزها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to cast the staff down; it becomes a serpent that moves quickly.
rows.anchor: فألقاها فإذا هي حية تسعى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the serpent as yellow with a horse-like crest, swelling until it became a great snake larger than ordinary serpents.
rows.anchor: صارت حية صفراء لها عرف كعرف الفرس وجعلت تتورم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account describes an enormous serpent crossing rock like a pregnant camel, swallowing it, uprooting a great tree with its fangs, fire in its eyes, and the staff's crook becoming a meteor-haired neck; Moses fled, then stopped from shame before God and returned when called, still terrified.
rows.anchor: بأعظم ثعبان نظر إليه الناظرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to take the serpent with his right hand without fear and promises to return it to its original state as a staff.
rows.anchor: ولا تخف سنعيدها سيرتها الأولى

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Moses wore a wool garment and initially covered his hand with its edge; God asked whether the garment could protect him if God allowed the danger. Moses admitted his weakness, uncovered his hand, and put it in the serpent's mouth, where it returned to its familiar place between the staff's prongs.
rows.anchor: وعلى موسى يومئذ مدرعة من صوف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the staff was myrtle from Paradise, brought by Adam and inherited by the prophets until Shu'ayb passed it to Moses.
rows.anchor: من آس الجنة أخرجها آدم ع وتوارثها الأنبياء

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the staff was from a thorny tree, ten cubits long and as tall as Moses.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: كانت من عوسج وكان طولها عشرة أذرع

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi take placing the hand by the wing to mean joining it to what is beneath the armpit.
rows.anchor: معناه واجمع يدك إلى ما تحت عضدك عن مجاهد والكلبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says to place the hand at the side; جناح is a figurative name for the side.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى جنبك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss says to put the hand into the garment's pocket, using جناح as a figure for the side.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أدخلها في جيبك وكنى عن الجنب بالجناح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The hand came out luminous, shining day and night like the sun and moon and even brighter.
rows.anchor: لها نور ساطع يضيء بالليل والنهار كضوء الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: الجميع
rows.claim: All commentators take من غير سوء to mean without leprosy; Moses was dark-complexioned, and his hand returned to its original color after the sign.
rows.anchor: من غير برص في قول الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آية أخرى can mean that God thereby adds another sign, or that the hand emerges manifestly as another sign.
rows.anchor: أي فنزيدك بها آية أخرى أو تخرج مبينة آية أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God will show Moses some of His proofs, described as the greatest.
rows.anchor: لنريك من آياتنا } وحججنا { الكبرى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural set of signs can be described by الكبرى in the singular; alternatively, the phrase means some of God's greatest proofs beyond the two signs just shown.
rows.anchor: ولو قال الكبر على الجمع وصفا لجميع الآيات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the greatest signs as the destruction of Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها هلاك فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After entrusting Moses with the mission and showing him the miracles, God commands him to call Pharaoh, who had become arrogant and tyrannical in disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي تجبر وتكبر في كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for an expanded heart so he will not become impatient, afraid, or distressed.
rows.anchor: وسع لي صدري حتى لا أضجر ولا أخاف ولا أغتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks God to ease the mission of entering the tyrant's presence and calling him to truth.
rows.anchor: سهل علي أداء ما كلفتني من الرسالة والدخول على الطاغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to release the knot in his tongue so his audience can understand him; he stuttered and could not articulate letters clearly.
rows.anchor: وأطلق عن لساني العقدة التي فيه حتى يفقهوا كلامي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: They attribute Moses' stammer to a coal burned in his mouth as a child: after he tugged Pharaoh's beard and Pharaoh wanted to kill him, Asiya argued he was too young to distinguish a jewel from an ember; Gabriel turned his hand to the coal.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed saying calls Moses a brother and says he killed a man by mistake; the text says he was twelve years old.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن اثنتي عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Moses from grief and fear after the killing, freeing him from anxiety over retaliation by the Copt and from fear.
rows.anchor: من غم القتل وكربه لأنه خاف أن يقتصوا منه بالقبطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested Moses as though dealing with someone under trial, until he was purified for prophetic selection; this was one of God's greatest favors to him.
rows.anchor: اختبرناك اختبارا ومعناه إنا عاملناك معاملة المختبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads it as rescuing Moses through successive ordeals: birth during the infanticide, the river, nursing only from his mother, tugging Pharaoh's beard, choosing a coal instead of a jewel and thereby avoiding death, then learning of the plot against him from a fellow partisan.
rows.anchor: ثم مجيء رجل من شيعته يسعى ليخبره بما عزموا عليه من قتله عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another gloss says God imposed hardship in earning a livelihood, so Moses shepherded for Shu'ayb for ten years.
rows.anchor: وشددنا عليك التعمد في أمر المعاش حتى رعيت لشعيب عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses spent those years among Shu'ayb's people as his shepherd.
rows.anchor: أي لبثت فيهم حين كنت راعيا لشعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means Moses came at the time appointed for his sending as a prophet.
rows.anchor: في الوقت الذي قدر لإرسالك نبيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation places his arrival at the time prophets receive revelation, when he was forty years old.
rows.anchor: على الوقت الذي يوحى إلى الأنبياء وهو على رأس أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he came at the measure God decreed and recorded in the Preserved Tablet for his speech, prophethood, and revelation.
rows.anchor: على المقدار الذي قدره الله لمجيئك وكتبه في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses this as choosing Moses for God's revelation and message; Tabrisi says he was made God's own and devoted to His will and love, since love is especially associated with the self.
rows.anchor: والمعنى اخترتك واتخذتك صنيعتي وأخلصتك لتنصرف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Moses was chosen to establish God's proof and placed between God and creation, occupying in conveying the message the position God would have in addressing and arguing with them.
rows.anchor: اخترتك لإقامة حجتي وجعلتك بيني وبين خلقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs here mean His proofs and evidences.
rows.anchor: أي بحججي ودلالاتي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the signs to mean the nine miracles.
rows.anchor: بالآيات التسع عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads this as not weakening in God's mission.
rows.anchor: أي ولا تضعفا في رسالتي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reads it as not slackening in God's command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولا تفترا في أمري عن السدي

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says not to fall short in God's command because fear of Pharaoh might make them slacken.
rows.anchor: ولا تقصرا عن محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to go to Pharaoh repeats the first for emphasis.
rows.anchor: كرر الأمر بالذهاب للتأكيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the first command addressed Moses alone, while the second addresses both brothers to make Aaron a prophet and partner in the mission.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن في الأول خص موسى بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the limit in tyranny.
rows.anchor: أي جاوز الحد في الطغيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to deal gently with Pharaoh in the invitation and not speak harshly.
rows.anchor: أي ارفقا به في الدعاء والقول ولا تغلظا له في ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي وعكرمة
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Ikrima interpret gentle speech as addressing Pharaoh by a kunya; views name Abu al-Walid, Abu al-Abbas, or Abu Marra.
rows.anchor: معناه كنياه عن السدي وعكرمة وكنيته أبو الوليد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies gentle speech with Moses' invitation to be purified and guided to his Lord, the wording quoted in 79:18–19.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القول اللين هو هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى عن مقاتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Moses offered Pharaoh Islam in exchange for lasting youth, kingship, bodily pleasures until death, and Paradise afterward; Pharaoh liked it but waited for Haman's counsel.
rows.anchor: تسلم وتؤمن برب العالمين على أن لك شبابك فلا تهرم

rows.speaker: هامان
rows.claim: Haman rebukes Pharaoh for wanting to move from being a lord to a subject and from being worshipped to worshipping, turning him away from accepting Moses' invitation.
rows.anchor: قد كنت أرى أن لك عقلا وأن لك رأيا

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh remarks that if this is the gentleness shown to someone claiming divinity, one should consider the gentleness due to someone claiming servitude.
rows.anchor: هذا رفقك بمن يدعي الربوبية فكيف رفقك بمن يدعي العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers are to call Pharaoh with hope that he will remember or fear, rather than despairing of his success; this posture is more effective in summoning him to truth.
rows.anchor: ادعواه على الرجاء والطمع لا على اليأس من فلاحه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj, following Sibawayh, explains the wording as 'go with your hope and expectation'; God knows the outcome, but messengers are sent hoping people accept.
rows.anchor: والمعنى في هذا عند سيبويه اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission's purpose is that Pharaoh recall God's lordship and his own servitude, and fear the punishment and warning.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيان الغرض بالبعثة أي ليتذكر ما أغفل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentleness in calling people to God, commanding right, and forbidding wrong helps them accept the message and keeps them from recoiling.
rows.anchor: يرفق في الدعاء إلى الله وفي الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Aaron was in Egypt; when Moses was told to come there, God instructed Aaron to meet him, and the brothers conferred and went to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: إن هارون كان بمصر فلما أوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى أن يأتي مصر

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwan reads تلقف with رفع; others use جزم, with Hafs reading it lightly and the rest doubling the قاف, while al-Bazzi's and Ibn Fulayh's transmissions from Ibn Kathir also double the initial تاء.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن ذكوان تلقف بالرفع والباقون بالجزم إلا أن حفصا يقرؤها خفيفة

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: The Kufans except Asim read كيد سحر without an alif; the others read ساحر with an alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ كيد سحر بغير ألف أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون ساحر بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The رفع reading treats the verb as a circumstantial clause, attributable either to the thrower or to the thrown object, the staff, feminine by sense; 99:4 offers a similar shift between human addressee and Earth as speaker.
rows.anchor: بالرفع فإنه يرتفع لأنه في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The جزم reading is a conditional answer: if you throw it, it will swallow them.
rows.anchor: فعلى أن يكون جوابا كأنه قال أن تلقه تلقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubling the تاء represents تتلقف and can be understood with either the human addressee or the feminine staff; Tabrisi notes that assimilation seems formally problematic because a sukun would call for a hamzat al-wasl unavailable in the present tense, and reports Ahmad ibn Musa's explanation that the reader begins as in the unassimilated form.
rows.anchor: ومن شدد التاء فإنما أراد تتلقف

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says لقفت الشيء and its forms mean to take something quickly.
rows.anchor: يقال لقفت الشيء وتلقفته والتقفته إذا أخذته بسرعة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says people in the Hijaz call a teacher كبير; in Arabic كبير means a leader or chief.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: الصبي في الحجاز إذا جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإيثار means choosing; تزكي means seeking growth or purification, and zakat is so named because wealth grows through it.
rows.anchor: والإيثار الإختيار والتزكي طلب الزكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن is separated from ما because ما is relative and صنعوا its clause, with a deleted resumptive; alternatively ما is a particle and the phrase means إن صنعهم.
rows.anchor: إن مفصول من ما صنعوا لأن ما ههنا موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آمنتم به uses the preposition باء for faith as the opposite of disbelief, while آمنتم له means believing or affirming someone.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين آمنتم به وآمنتم له إن آمنتم به بالباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من can mean عن, yielding 'from opposite sides,' or على, yielding 'on opposite sides'; the prepositional phrase is an accusative circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون من بمعنى عن أي عن خلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here في means على, 'on the palm trunks,' because the trunks surround the victims and so they are described as being inside them.
rows.anchor: في بمعنى على وإنما جاز ذلك لأن الجذع قد اشتمل عليهم
